mainTopic: Selling a spoiling deposit: the משנה's מחלוקת, the reasons of רב כהנא and רב נחמן בר יצחק, and רבי יוחנן's limit to normal loss
overview: The amud opens by closing the previous discussion: both cases in that משנה follow the רבנן, taught in a 'not only this, but also that' style. Then a new משנה begins. If deposited produce is spoiling, the תנא קמא says the שומר may not touch it, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he sells it in בית דין. רב כהנא explains that a person prefers his own produce. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the owner may already have made it תרומה ומעשר for other produce. רבי יוחנן limits the argument to normal loss: if the produce loses more than normal, everyone agrees it is sold. The גמרא shows this fits רב כהנא but not רב נחמן בר יצחק. It explains that such a sale goes to כהנים at the price of תרומה, and that the two sides disagree about how common and how early extra loss is. A ברייתא with רבי מאיר and the חכמים is then brought as a challenge, and the גמרא answers it. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a new question about oil and honey, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's reason applies to both cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on an earlier suggestion that one case in the previous משנה was needed to teach something about רבי יוסי's view. רבי יוסי's reason is to make the cheater lose out, and that reason applies the same way everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't רבי יוסי's reason because of the loss to the cheater?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is knocking down the previous answer about why the משנה needed two similar cases. It points out that רבי יוסי's reason does not depend on the details of either case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer assumed רבי יוסי might rule differently in one case than in the other. But רבי יוסי's stated reason is to make sure the cheater gains nothing. That reason works equally in both cases, so there is no room for him to agree in one and disagree in the other.

phrases.english: But isn't the reason of Rabbi Yosei
phrases.notes: In the earlier משנה, רבי יוסי said all the money stays put until אליהו comes, so the cheater loses too.

phrases.english: because of the loss to the cheater?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given just before this section about why the משנה lists two cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier claim that one case was needed to show רבי יוסי's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's reason (the cheater's loss) applies equally in both cases, so neither case can teach a special point about him.

steps.title: Both cases follow the רבנן, taught as 'not only this but also that'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. Both cases are needed for the רבנן's view, and the משנה uses the style of 'not only this, but also that.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both cases are needed according to the רבנן, and the משנה teaches in the style of 'not only this, but even that.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected answer with a new one. It explains why the משנה lists two cases even though one could be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases belong to the רבנן, not to רבי יוסי. The משנה starts with the more obvious case and then adds the more surprising one. This is a known teaching style, so the extra case is not a waste of words.

keyTerms.meaning: not only this, but also that: a teaching style that moves from the obvious case to the newer one

steps.whatToRemember: When one case seems to make another unnecessary, the גמרא can answer 'לא זו אף זו': the משנה builds from the easier case to the bigger חידוש.

phrases.english: Rather, both are needed according to the Rabbis,
and it teaches 'not only this, but also that.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 1 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns both cases to the רבנן and explains the doubling as a teaching style.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One case was needed to show something about רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are for the רבנן, written as 'לא זו אף זו'.

steps.title: משנה: deposited produce that is going bad
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. If produce deposited with a שומר is spoiling, the תנא קמא says he may not touch it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he sells it in בית דין, because that is like returning a lost item.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone deposits produce with his friend, even if it is getting ruined, the friend may not touch it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he sells it in front of בית דין, because he is like someone returning a lost item to its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a מחלוקת. The question is what a שומר should do when the deposited produce is going bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says to leave the produce alone, even though it is losing value. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says to sell it through בית דין and keep the money for the owner. In his view, saving the value is like returning a lost item.

keyTerms.meaning: one who deposits (gives an item to someone to guard)
being lost, here meaning spoiling or losing value

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבודין' here does not mean the produce disappeared. It means the produce is spoiling or shrinking while it sits there.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who deposits produce with his friend,
even if it is getting lost (spoiling),
he may not touch it.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He sells it in front of the court,
because he is like one returning a lost item to the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the שומר may not touch spoiling deposited produce. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: he sells it in בית דין, as a form of השבת אבידה.

steps.title: Why may the bailee not touch it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא forbids the שומר from selling produce that is spoiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the תנא קמא's ruling. It is setting up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems obvious that selling spoiling produce helps the owner. So the גמרא wants to know why the תנא קמא forbids it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the first view in the משנה: why not let him sell it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the תנא קמא's ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the תנא קמא forbids selling deposited produce that is spoiling.

steps.title: רב כהנא: a person prefers his own
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says that a person would rather have one קב of his own produce than nine קבים of someone else's. So the owner wants his own produce left alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: A person prefers one קב of his own over nine קבים of his friend's.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives the first answer. The owner cares about keeping his own produce, even if less of it is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שומר sold it, the owner would get money or other produce back instead of his own. Since people value their own produce much more, the owner would rather keep what is left of his. So the שומר should leave it alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saying about how people value what is their own is the basis for the תנא קמא's ruling here. The גמרא will soon test how far it goes, and whether it covers produce that loses more than its normal amount.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
A person prefers a kav of his own
to nine kav of his friend's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָדָם רוֹצֶה בְּקַב שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner prefers to keep his own produce, so the שומר may not sell it.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the owner may have used it as תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different reason. Maybe the owner already made this produce the תרומה ומעשר for his other produce somewhere else, so a buyer might eat it wrongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We are worried that perhaps the depositor made it תרומה ומעשר for produce in another place.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reason for the same ruling. His reason is a worry about איסור, not about the owner's feelings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner, relying on the produce being where he left it, may have declared it תרומה or מעשר for his other produce. If the שומר sells it, a buyer could end up eating תרומה or מעשר as if it were regular food. That is why the שומר must not touch it.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of produce given to a כהן
tithe, a tenth of the produce

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We are concerned that perhaps the depositor made them
terumah and tithe for another place.
phrases.notes: He means the owner set aside this stored produce as the תרומה for his other produce elsewhere.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The produce may already be תרומה ומעשר for other produce, so selling it could cause a buyer to eat it improperly.

steps.title: A ברייתא: therefore the owner may make it תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It says the שומר may not touch the produce, and 'therefore' the owner may make it תרומה ומעשר for produce elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: One who deposits produce with his friend, the friend may not touch it. Therefore the owner makes it תרומה ומעשר for another place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to test the two answers. This step is the setup; the actual test comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the rules in a specific order. First, the שומר may not touch the produce. Then, because of that ('לפיכך'), the owner may use it as תרומה for elsewhere. The key word is 'לפיכך', since it tells us which rule causes which.

phrases.english: They challenged: One who deposits produce with his friend,
this one may not touch it.
Therefore the owner makes them
terumah and tithe for another place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the two reasons given in steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason of רב נחמן בר יצחק (step 6).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the owner's power to make the produce תרומה as a result ('לפיכך') of the no-touching rule, not as its cause.

steps.title: The word 'therefore' fits רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא's word 'לפיכך' makes sense for רב כהנא. This prepares the challenge against רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רב כהנא; that is why it says 'therefore.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא fits רב כהנא's reason. It is setting up the next move, which will question how the ברייתא fits רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב כהנא, the no-touching rule comes from the owner's wish to keep his own produce. Since the produce is sure to stay put, it follows ('therefore') that the owner can safely make it תרומה for elsewhere. For רב נחמן בר יצחק, the תרומה worry is the cause of the rule, so 'therefore' seems backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: granted, it works well (for one view, setting up a problem for the other)

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא לרב כהנא' is not the end of the discussion. It sets up a coming problem for רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Kahana,
this is why it teaches 'therefore.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב כָּהֲנָא הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי לְפִיכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא of step 7 and shows it fits רב כהנא, preparing a challenge to רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's reason for the no-touching rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's word 'לפיכך', which presents the owner's power to make the produce תרומה as a result of the no-touching rule.

steps.title: What does 'therefore' mean for רב נחמן בר יצחק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק: how does the word 'לפיכך' in the ברייתא fit his reason?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב נחמן בר יצחק, what does 'therefore' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רב נחמן בר יצחק and asks how the word 'לפיכך' fits his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב כהנא the order is simple: the produce stays untouched, so the owner can use it as תרומה ומעשר. For רב נחמן בר יצחק the order looks backwards. The owner possibly making it תרומה ומעשר is the reason the שומר can't sell, so 'therefore' seems to point the wrong way.

keyTerms.meaning: therefore; this follows as a result

phrases.english: But according to רב נחמן בר יצחק,
what is the meaning of 'therefore'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַאי לְפִיכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast set up in Step 8: 'לפיכך' fits רב כהנא, but what about רב נחמן בר יצחק?
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes being allowed to designate תרומה a result of not selling. רב נחמן בר יצחק makes it the cause of not selling.

steps.title: Since he may not sell, the owner can rely on the produce being there
steps.stepSummary: Once the חכמים forbade selling because of the תרומה worry, the owner can count on the produce still being there. So he may make it תרומה ומעשר for elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: now that the רבנן said he may not sell, because we are worried, therefore the owner may make it תרומה and מעשר for produce in another place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב נחמן בר יצחק by rereading the ברייתא so that 'לפיכך' makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about תרומה led the חכמים to make a rule that the שומר never sells. Because of that rule, the owner can be sure his produce is still with the שומר. So he may use it as תרומה ומעשר even from the start. The 'therefore' points to the security the rule gives the owner.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Now that the Rabbis said he may not sell,
because we are concerned —
therefore the owner may make them
תרומה and מעשר for produce in another place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: 'לפיכך' refers to the result of the חכמים' rule, not of the original worry.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לפיכך' contradicts רב נחמן בר יצחק, because for him the תרומה worry is the cause.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry causes the rule against selling. The rule then lets the owner confidently designate the produce, so 'לפיכך' works for both opinions.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב כהנא and רב נחמן בר יצחק can explain the ברייתא's 'לפיכך'.

steps.title: The dispute is only about normal loss
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the argument in the משנה is only when the produce loses its normal amount. If it loses more than normal, everyone agrees the שומר sells it in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the argument is when the produce is losing its normal amount. But if it is losing more than its normal amount, everyone agrees he sells it in court.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement limits where the argument in the משנה applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן splits the case in two. With normal loss, the תנא קמא says don't sell and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says sell. With extra loss beyond normal, all agree: sell it in בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: in court, under the court's supervision

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said:
The dispute is when they lose their normal amount,
phrases.notes: Stored produce normally shrinks a bit over time. That is the 'normal loss'.

phrases.english: but if they lose more than their normal amount —
everyone agrees that he sells them in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַחֲלוֹקֶת בִּכְדֵי חֶסְרוֹנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the exact scope of the משנה's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With normal loss there is a dispute. With more than normal loss, all agree the שומר sells in בית דין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical line. Fast spoiling must be sold in בית דין by everyone's opinion.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן argue with רב כהנא too?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן clearly argues with רב נחמן בר יצחק. The גמרא asks whether he also argues with רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: With רב נחמן בר יצחק, he certainly argues. Shall we say he argues with רב כהנא too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks how רבי יוחנן's rule fits each of the two earlier reasons, and sets up a question about רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry that the owner made it תרומה applies no matter how fast the produce spoils. So רב נחמן בר יצחק would forbid selling even with extra loss, which clashes with רבי יוחנן. The question is whether רב כהנא's 'owner prefers his own produce' also clashes.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק – וַדַּאי פְּלִיגָא.
phrases.english: With רב נחמן בר יצחק — it certainly disagrees.
Shall we say it disagrees with רב כהנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 11 with the two reasons from Steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי יוחנן's limit consistent with רב כהנא's reason?

steps.title: רב כהנא was only talking about normal loss
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא's reason was said only about normal loss. So he agrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב כהנא said it, he said it about normal loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב כהנא and רבי יוחנן do not argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner prefers his own produce only when it loses a normal amount. If it spoils faster than normal, even רב כהנא agrees the שומר should sell.

phrases.english: When רב כהנא said it —
he said it about their normal loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא בִּכְדֵי חֶסְרוֹנָן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב כהנא's reason is limited to normal loss, so he fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: But he said one קב over nine!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רב כהנא spoke of preferring one קב of his own over nine of another's. That sounds like huge loss, not normal loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said a person wants one קב of his own more than nine קבים of his friend's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by pointing to רב כהנא's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going from nine down to one means losing eight-ninths, which is far more than normal loss. That suggests רב כהנא holds the owner wants his own produce kept even with extreme loss, which would clash with רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: But surely he said: one wants a קב of his own
more than nine קבים of his fellow's!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רוֹצֶה בְּקַב שֶׁלּוֹ מִתִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב כהנא spoke only about normal loss
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own example describes losing eight-ninths, which is far beyond normal loss.

steps.title: It was just an exaggeration
steps.stepSummary: The 'one קב versus nine' was just a figure of speech, not an exact amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just an exaggeration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב כהנא's numbers were not meant literally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One קב over nine' is only a strong way of saying people love their own things. It does not mean the owner would accept huge loss. So רב כהנא still speaks only about normal loss and agrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן limits the dispute to normal loss. רב כהנא fits this rule because his 'nine קבים' was an exaggeration. רב נחמן בר יצחק does not fit it.

phrases.english: It is merely an exaggeration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Non-literal reading: the numbers are a figure of speech.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב כהנא meant the owner prefers his own produce even with huge loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: The numbers are an exaggeration. רב כהנא only speaks about normal loss, matching רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא lets the owner rely on the stored produce, so a sale could leave him eating טבלים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the owner may make the stored produce תרומה ומעשר for produce in another place. If the שומר might sell it when it loses more than normal, the owner could be eating טבלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'Therefore the owner may make it תרומה ומעשר for produce in another place.' But we should worry: maybe it lost more than its normal amount, the שומר sold it, and now the owner is eating טבלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן's rule that the שומר sells produce that loses more than normal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the stored produce is always still there, so the owner can count on it for his תרומה ומעשר. Under רבי יוחנן, the שומר might have sold it already. Then the owner's separation would take effect on nothing, and the produce at home that he eats would still be טבלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and מעשר were not yet taken; forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: The owner is not at the שומר's place. He separates תרומה ומעשר from far away, counting on the stored produce. That is why he wouldn't know if it was sold.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Therefore the owner may make them
terumah and tithe for produce in another place.
But let us worry that perhaps they came to have
more than their normal loss, and he sold them,
and the owner is eating untithed produce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that produce losing more than normal is sold in בית דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes the produce is always available for the owner's separation. A possible sale would make that separation empty, and the owner would eat טבלים.

steps.title: Losing more than the normal amount is rare
steps.stepSummary: Extra loss is uncommon, so the ברייתא doesn't worry about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Losing more than the normal amount is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that extra loss rarely happens, so the owner may rely on the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was written for the usual case, where the produce only loses its normal amount and is never sold. A rare case does not stop the owner from relying on it.

phrases.english: More than the normal loss is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rarity: the problem case is uncommon, so it is not a concern.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sale could happen at any time, so the owner can't rely on the produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: Extra loss is rare, so the owner may normally rely on the produce.

steps.title: When extra loss does happen, selling it is still a problem
steps.stepSummary: If extra loss does happen, do we sell? But the owner may have already made it תרומה ומעשר for produce elsewhere!
steps.simpleTranslation: And if extra loss is found, what then? Do we sell it? But we should worry that maybe the owner already made it תרומה ומעשר for produce in another place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further: in the rare case where extra loss does happen, selling still seems risky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if it is rare, רבי יוחנן says to sell in that case. The produce may already be תרומה, because the owner may have designated it. Selling it to anyone as regular food would be a problem.

phrases.english: And if it is found, what then?
phrases.notes: He means: if the produce really did lose more than its normal amount.

phrases.english: Do we sell them?
But let us worry that perhaps the owner made them
terumah and tithe for produce in another place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that extra loss is rare (Step 17), but challenges the ruling for the case when it does happen.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's instruction to sell in the case of extra loss.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The produce might already be תרומה, so an ordinary sale could cause non-כהנים to eat תרומה.

steps.title: The produce is sold to כהנים at the price of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The sale is made only to כהנים, at the lower price of תרומה, so it doesn't matter if it is תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when we sell it, we sell it to כהנים at the price of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sale is set up to be safe: it goes to כהנים at the price of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner did make it תרומה, כהנים may eat it, so nobody is harmed. Charging only the price of תרומה makes sure the כהן doesn't overpay in case it really is תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: The price of תרומה (cheaper, since only כהנים can buy it)

phrases.english: Even when we sell,
we sell them to priests at the price of terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical solution: the sale is limited so that it works even if the produce is תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling would risk non-כהנים eating תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Selling only to כהנים at the price of תרומה removes the risk.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב נחמן בר יצחק allow this same sale?
steps.stepSummary: If selling to כהנים solves the worry about תרומה, רב נחמן בר יצחק should also allow selling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב נחמן בר יצחק too, let us sell it to כהנים at the price of תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רב נחמן בר יצחק, who forbade selling because the owner may have made it תרומה. It asks why he doesn't accept the same fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason for not selling was the worry about the owner's תרומה. Selling to כהנים seems to answer that worry completely. So it is unclear why he still forbids a sale.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak as well,
let us sell them to priests at the price of terumah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the solution from Step 19 to challenge רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's refusal to allow a sale.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His stated worry about תרומה is solved by selling to כהנים, so his reason to forbid the sale seems to fall away.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה's view: extra loss is rare and comes only later
steps.stepSummary: The real dispute is about how common extra loss is and when it starts. For רבה בר בר חנה, any separation by the owner came before the extra loss, so selling to כהנים is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they argue about. רבה בר בר חנה holds that extra loss is not common at all. When it does happen, it only happens later on. If the owner made the produce תרומה ומעשר for produce elsewhere, he did it before the extra loss began. So when extra loss happens, we sell it to כהנים at the price of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sides disagree about the facts of extra loss. It first explains the side that allows a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה בר בר חנה, extra loss shows up only late. By then, the owner has already done any separating he planned. The only worry left is that the produce is already תרומה, and selling to כהנים handles that.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they argue about

phrases.english: It is about this that they disagree:
for Rabba bar bar Ḥana holds:
phrases.notes: רבה בר בר חנה is the one who reported רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 11, so this is that side of the argument.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי חֶסְרוֹנָן לָא שְׁכִיחַ מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: more than the normal loss is not common at all,
and when it does happen,
it is only later on that it becomes
more than the normal loss.
If the owner made them
terumah and tithe for produce in another place,
it was before they came to have
more than the normal loss that he made them so.
Therefore, when they come to have
more than the normal loss,
let us sell them to priests at the price of terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by explaining the side that allows a sale.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual dispute: the two sides disagree about how often extra loss happens and when.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling to כהנים should satisfy everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Selling to כהנים is enough only if the owner's separation surely came before the sale. רבה בר בר חנה holds that it did.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק's view: extra loss is common and can come right away
steps.stepSummary: Extra loss can happen right away, so the שומר might sell before the owner separates. The owner, not knowing, would then eat טבלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק holds that extra loss is common, and it can start right away. If you say we sell it, sometimes the שומר will sell it early. Then, when the owner makes it תרומה ומעשר for produce elsewhere, he won't know it was sold, and he will be eating טבלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by explaining why רב נחמן בר יצחק still forbids a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling to כהנים only solves the case where the owner separated before the sale. If the sale can come early, the owner may later separate on produce that is already gone. Then his separation does nothing, and he eats טבלים. Selling to כהנים cannot fix that.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that selling to כהנים fixes the worry that the produce is already תרומה. They disagree about whether a sale might come before the owner separates. רבה בר בר חנה says no, since extra loss is rare and late, so we sell. רב נחמן בר יצחק says yes, since it is common and can be immediate, so we don't sell, or the owner may eat טבלים.

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak holds:
more than the normal loss is indeed common,
and when they come to have it,
it can be right away that they have it.
And if you say, let us sell them,
sometimes he will act early and sell them,
and when the owner makes them
terumah and tithe for produce in another place,
he does not know that it was sold,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets belongs to the corrected wording, so read it as 'it was sold.'

phrases.english: and he ends up eating untithed produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 21 by giving רב נחמן בר יצחק's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual dispute: extra loss is common and can be immediate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling to כהנים removes every concern.
steps.terutzMaskana: An early sale could come before the owner separates, leaving him eating טבלים, so רב נחמן בר יצחק forbids selling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement depends on how common extra loss is and how early it can happen, which decides whether the owner's separation might come after a sale.

steps.title: A ברייתא about spoiling deposits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says the שומר may not touch spoiling deposits. חכמים say he sells them in בית דין, but only to others and never to himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Someone deposited produce with his friend and it rotted, or wine that turned sour, oil that went rancid, or honey that spoiled. The friend may not touch them, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say he fixes the situation and sells them in court. When he sells them, he sells to others and not to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to set up a challenge against רבה בר בר חנה. The actual attack comes in step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is like our משנה, but here the opinion against selling belongs to רבי מאיר. The list of items, especially wine, oil and honey, will be used to show which kind of loss is being discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: It went rancid / began to smell
He makes a fix for them, meaning he saves their value

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who deposits produce with his friend and it rotted,
wine and it turned sour, oil and it went rancid,
honey and it spoiled –
he may not touch them,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the Sages say: he makes a fix for them,
and sells them in court.
And when he sells them –
he sells them to others
and does not sell them to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמַּפְקִיד פֵּירוֹת אֵצֶל חֲבֵירוֹ וְהִרְקִיבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to test רבה בר בר חנה's claim that everyone agrees to sell when the loss is beyond normal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the שומר does not touch spoiling deposits. חכמים: he sells them in בית דין, to others only.

steps.title: Similar cases with charity collectors
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds similar rules. Charity collectors may exchange or sell charity items for others, but not for themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly: charity collectors with no poor people to give to exchange the coins for others, but not for themselves. Collectors for the food plate with no poor people to give to sell the food to others, but not to themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with two more cases that follow the same rule: do not deal with yourself, so nobody suspects you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the שומר, a person handling public money must avoid any appearance of benefiting himself. This part does not affect the coming challenge. The גמרא quotes it because it is part of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly, a case that follows the same idea
They exchange small coins for bigger ones
Charity plate, a public food distribution

phrases.english: Similarly: charity collectors
at a time when they have no poor people to distribute to –
exchange the coins for others,
phrases.notes: They swap lots of small copper coins for silver ones, which last better until poor people come.

phrases.english: but do not exchange them for themselves.
Collectors for the charity plate
at a time when they have no poor people to distribute to –
sell the food to others,
but do not sell it to themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted ברייתא with parallel cases of avoiding suspicion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Charity collectors may exchange or sell charity items to others, but not to themselves.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר forbid selling even with extra loss?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'produce that rotted.' That sounds like it includes loss beyond the normal rate. Yet רבי מאיר still says don't touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it teaches 'produce and it rotted.' Doesn't that mean even more than its normal loss?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes its attack. Rotting sounds like more than normal loss, and still רבי מאיר says not to sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה said the argument is only about normal loss, and with extra loss everyone agrees to sell. If רבי מאיר forbids selling even with extra loss, then there is someone who argues, and רבה בר בר חנה's 'everyone agrees' is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (pushing toward a reading)
More than their normal expected loss

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches 'produce and it rotted,'

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו אֲפִילּוּ יָתֵר מִכְּדֵי חֶסְרוֹנָן?
phrases.english: isn't it even more than their normal loss?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא quoted in step 23 to attack רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר בר חנה's claim that with loss beyond normal, everyone agrees to sell in בית דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Rotted' suggests extra loss. רבי מאיר still forbids touching, so not everyone agrees to sell.

steps.title: No, the produce case is normal loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'rotted' in the ברייתא means only the normal amount of loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means at their normal rate of loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The rotting produce is only losing the usual amount, so רבי מאיר's 'don't touch' says nothing about extra loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is only about normal loss, it fits רבה בר בר חנה. The argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים is about normal loss, and extra loss is a separate case where all agree.

keyTerms.meaning: At their normal expected rate of loss

phrases.english: No, at their normal loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to normal loss
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Rotted' means extra loss, so רבי מאיר forbids selling even then.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce is only at normal loss. That is where רבי מאיר and חכמים argue.

steps.title: Wine, oil and honey are clearly extra loss
steps.stepSummary: Wine turning sour, oil going rancid and honey spoiling are clearly big losses, more than normal. Yet רבי מאיר says don't touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wine that turned sour, oil that went rancid and honey that spoiled are more than their normal loss!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The other items in the same list are obviously extra loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sour wine or rancid oil is worth far less than before. That is surely more than normal loss. Since רבי מאיר says don't touch these too, it seems he forbids selling even with extra loss.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it... (introducing a challenge)

phrases.english: But wine and it turned sour,
oil and it went rancid, honey and it spoiled –
these are more than their normal loss!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 26 using the other items in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא deals only with normal loss.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wine, oil and honey in the same list clearly show extra loss, and רבי מאיר still says don't touch.

steps.title: Once spoiled, they stay that way
steps.stepSummary: Wine, oil and honey are different. Once they have spoiled, they don't keep getting worse, so selling them saves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are different. Once they reach that state, they stay that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי מאיר says don't touch the wine, oil and honey even though their loss was big. The damage is already done and will not grow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling in בית דין is meant to stop future loss. Sour wine stays sour and does not keep dropping in value, so selling would save nothing. רבי מאיר's 'don't touch' here does not prove he forbids selling when the loss is still growing beyond normal.

keyTerms.meaning: Once it stands, it stands; once it spoils, it stays at that level

steps.whatToRemember: רבה בר בר חנה survives the challenge. In the ברייתא, the produce is losing only the normal amount. The wine, oil and honey had a big loss, but it has stopped, so selling would not help. Neither case is ongoing extra loss.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying sour wine is only normal loss. It admits the loss was big. The point is that the loss has stopped, and selling only makes sense to prevent future loss.

phrases.english: These are different,
since once they reach that state, they stay.
phrases.notes: Literally 'once it stood, it stood'. The spoiled item stops losing value, so there is nothing more to save.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 and closes the challenge against רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the loss is finished, not ongoing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wine, oil and honey prove that רבי מאיר forbids selling even with extra loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their loss has stopped, so selling gains nothing. רבי מאיר's ruling says nothing about ongoing extra loss.

steps.title: Quoting oil and honey to set up a new question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'oil that went rancid, honey that spoiled' again to begin a new question about these cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Oil and it went rancid, honey and it spoiled –
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes these words from the ברייתא again to prepare a new question, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא just said spoiled items stay as they are. Now it focuses on oil and honey specifically to ask something more about them. The question itself continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Oil and it went rancid, honey and it spoiled –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts with a quote from the ברייתא to open a new question about oil and honey.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question about oil and honey continues on the next amud.
